title: The rhythm of syllables
summary: Learn to tell stressed and unstressed syllables apart in Spanish words.
keyIdeas: In these example words, the stressed syllable is pronounced more strongly.
The other syllables in these examples are unstressed and pronounced less strongly.
Saying a word naturally helps you recognise its stress.

basicKnowledge: D. Reflexión sobre la lengua y sus usos en el marco de propuestas de producción y comprensión de textos orales, escritos o multimodales

activities.prompt: Aisha explains a stressed syllable to her brother. Which explanation is correct?
activities.explanation: A stressed syllable is the syllable given the strongest emphasis in a word.
activities.hint: Think of which syllable sounds strongest when you speak.
options: Any syllable without a written accent mark.
Always the first syllable of a word.
The syllable pronounced most strongly in a word.

activities.prompt: The Spanish word «cartera» has two stressed syllables.
activities.explanation: In «car-te-ra», only «te» is stressed. «car» and «ra» are unstressed.

activities.prompt: Hugo says the Spanish word «cartera» («car-te-ra») aloud. 🎒 Which syllable is stressed?
activities.explanation: The strongest emphasis in «car-te-ra» falls on «te».
activities.hint: Imagine calling the word from far away: «¡car-TEE-ra!».

activities.prompt: Complete the Spanish sentence with the correct word.
activities.explanation: Unstressed syllables are pronounced less strongly, without the word's main stress.
activities.sentence: Las sílabas de una palabra que se pronuncian con menos fuerza se llaman sílabas ___.

activities.prompt: Match each Spanish word to its stressed syllable.
activities.explanation: The stress falls on these syllables: «plá» in «plá-ta-no», «loj» in «re-loj», «ta» in «ven-ta-na» and «mú» in «mú-si-ca».

activities.prompt: Sort these Spanish words by the position of their stressed syllable.
activities.explanation: «balón», «papel» and «ratón» have final stress. «mesa», «árbol» and «mochila» have stress on the second-last syllable.

activities.prompt: Lucía marks the stressed syllable in capitals in four Spanish words. Which one has a mistake?
activities.explanation: «PA-pel» is incorrect. Say «pa-PEL», so «pel» is stressed, rather than «pa».
activities.hint: Say «papel» naturally to hear where the stress falls.

activities.prompt: Read the Spanish text and answer the questions.
activities.explanation: The story uses a calling trick to stretch the stressed syllable and tell it apart from the unstressed syllables.
activities.title: El juego del caza-sílabas
activities.text: Hoy en clase de tercero hemos jugado al «caza-sílabas». La maestra Clara nos ha enseñado un truco muy divertido: para encontrar la sílaba tónica de cualquier palabra, debemos imaginar que llamamos a alguien desde la otra punta del patio. Martina lo probó primero con la palabra «manzana»: gritó «¡man-ZAAA-na!» y todos escuchamos enseguida que la sílaba «za» sonaba con más fuerza y duración. Después, Omar probó con «tambor»: gritó «¡tam-BOOOR!» y descubrió que la sílaba tónica era «bor». ¡Nadie falló en toda la tarde!

questions.prompt: What trick does teacher Clara suggest for finding the stressed syllable?
questions.explanation: The text suggests imagining that you are calling someone from the other end of the playground.
options: Write the word with a green pen.
Count the word's letters on your fingers.
Pretend to call someone from far away.

questions.prompt: How many unstressed syllables are in the Spanish word «manzana»?
questions.explanation: «manzana» has three syllables: «man-za-na». «za» is stressed, so «man» and «na» are unstressed.

activities.prompt: Put Adrián's steps in order to find the unstressed syllables in one of these example words.
activities.explanation: First split into syllables, find the stressed syllable and identify the remaining syllables as unstressed.
items: Say the word to find the strongest emphasis.
Identify the remaining syllables as unstressed.

activities.prompt: Nerea makes a word list for the school newspaper. She wants two Spanish words with stress on the last syllable. Which pair should she choose?
activities.explanation: «le-ón» and «pa-red» have final stress. «casa» has stress on the second-last syllable, and «plátano» on the third-last.
activities.hint: Check the stress in both words of each pair.
